Axios Closer
By Nathan Bomey · Nov 12, 2026

Thursday ✅.

Today's newsletter is 663 words, a 2½-minute read.

📉 The dashboard: The S&P 500 closed down 0.4%.

  • Oil prices rose as hopes fade for a near-term end to the Iran war, and bond yields surged on Tuesday's hot inflation report and growing expectations for rate hikes.

👀 Today's stock spotlight: Anthropic's IPO is reportedly six times oversubscribed — a sign of surging interest in the AI model developer as Nvidia shares continue their retreat.
 
 
1 big thing: Jensen Jenga
 

Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios
 

Jensen Huang's self-destruction has left a trail of collateral damage that threatens to ensnare the board of Nvidia and the AI boom itself.

  • Huang resigned this morning as CEO of the world's most important chipmaker.
  • His sudden exit after reports of multiple affairs — one with a suspected Chinese spy and the other with a direct report — has wiped out more than $600 billion in value from Nvidia's market cap.

🌐 Why it matters: Huang was a singular leader in the global economy, capable of exciting or calming markets with a single sentence and viewed as a virtually indestructible force behind Nvidia's rise.

  • "His visionary leadership is going to be missed — it's not going to be replaced," Joel Shulman, CEO of ERShares, which has owned Nvidia shares since 2005, tells Axios.

🧐 Attention will now quickly pivot to a slew of unanswered questions, including:

🔍 What will the investigations uncover?

  • Just because he's gone doesn't mean this is over. If the FBI probe or the independent investigation ordered by the board show that Huang gave favorable treatment to Megaspeed — the company led by the suspected spy Alice Huang — he and Nvidia could face serious consequences.
  • Huang is also expected to testify behind closed doors next week before a congressional committee.

🎈 Could this be the catalyst that pops the AI bubble?

  • Nvidia is the backbone of the global AI economy, with its chips, investments and financial guarantees sustaining an entire ecosystem of companies worth trillions of dollars — and Huang is at the center of that vast flywheel, Axios' Zachary Basu writes.

Next week becomes a "critical" moment with Tuesday's Nvidia earnings report and Thursday's likely Anthropic IPO, Shulman says.

  • This Nvidia story is going to take a little air out of the balloon for the Anthropic IPO," he says.

Go deeper
 
 
2. When the chips are down
 
Data: Financial Modeling Prep; Chart: Pete Gannon/Axios

Nvidia shares closed down another 4.3% today and are down nearly 27% over the last month, having lost about $1 trillion in value.

  • 🗣️ "With this kind of leadership uncertainty, it's very difficult to predict where shares go over the next several trading sessions," writes Ken Mahoney, CEO of Mahoney Asset Management. "Sometimes huge news catalysts like this take all technicals out of the equation."

Follow the money: Will Huang's exit fundamentally reshape the long-term competitive landscape of the chip industry?

  • Competitors like AMD, Alphabet, Broadcom and Intel could benefit if chips customers are soured on working with Nvidia.
  • "When a star leaves a Wall Street firm, the first question is always the same: Did the clients sign with the banker — or with the bank? Nvidia is about to answer that question on the biggest stage in the market," writes Mark Malek, CIO at Siebert Financial.
 
 
3. 🗞️ The readout
 

Photo: SpaceX via Getty Images
 

🤝 Merger talks between SpaceX and Tesla are reportedly progressing, and Elon Musk's companies could announce a deal as soon as December. (Bloomberg)

🔮 Donald Trump Jr. will no longer be an advisor to Kalshi, in what the prediction market called a mutual decision after his VC firm invested in Kalshi competitor Polymarket. (CNBC)

💻 Microsoft was experiencing a widespread outage this afternoon, with Outlook among the apps affected. (NBC News)
